title: Heart of Three
concept: A thin heart outline is threaded through the three Julia dots — purple & green at the lobes, red at the point — so the heart is drawn *by* the triad, not beside it.
why: A whole heart emerges from just three dots and a hairline stroke: minimum ink, maximum recognition.
risk: Departs from the canonical one-up/two-down arrangement; the cut heart can shrink at 32px.

title: Rhythm Strip Classic
concept: Three P-QRS-T complexes on a running ECG baseline; each R-peak tip is capped by a Julia dot, so the dots literally *are* the heartbeats.
why: The most literal fusion of 'Julia dots' and 'heartbeat' — reads both ways instantly.
risk: Closest to a generic ECG logo; differentiation rests on the exact dot placement.

title: Pulse Orbit
concept: A limit-cycle ring doubles as a heartbeat: its lower arc between the red and green dots interrupts into a small QRS spike.
why: Single most literal fusion of HRV (the spike) and phase-space (the ring) — reads as both at once.
risk: The QRS spike is small relative to the ring and softens first at 32px.

title: Groove
concept: Three dots fused into a row with a full PQRST zigzag channel cut straight through them as bright negative space.
why: Strongest, most scientifically honest ECG read in the lane while staying pure negative space.
risk: Row layout departs furthest from the canonical triangle; colors carry the identity.

title: IBI Comb
concept: A row of vertical ticks with deliberately irregular spacing (an RR-interval comb); three thicker ticks are dot-capped.
why: Irregular tick spacing is honest shorthand for 'variability' — the core HRV concept, with near-zero clutter.
risk: Thin gray filler ticks can recede at tiny sizes, leaving 3 dots-on-sticks.

title: Limit-Cycle Ring
concept: A thin closed orbit threads through the three dots as if they were bodies riding a stable limit cycle; an arrowhead marks travel.
why: One continuous stroke reads instantly as 'orbit', and the triad sits exactly where the Julia mark expects it.
risk: The directional arrowhead is subtle and may vanish at 16px.

title: Return Map Minimal
concept: A minimal Poincaré return map: axes, a dashed identity diagonal, a lean SD1/SD2 cloud, and three dots stretched along the diagonal.
why: The most scientifically honest Poincaré plot in the lane while still reading as three Julia dots.
risk: Diagonal arrangement can parse as 'just a scatter plot' to someone who doesn't know the Julia mark.

title: Interval Calipers
concept: Three beats as beads on a rhythm line; unequal double-arrow brackets beneath measure the gaps — HRV as literally unequal intervals.
why: Directly visualizes the package's core measurement (the ⟷ interval), which nothing else does as explicitly.
risk: The caliper arrows are the smallest detail and soften first under downscaling.

title: Heart Cut
concept: The canonical tightly-overlapping triad with a small heart masked out of the negative space exactly where the three dots meet.
why: First read is 'three Julia dots'; second read reveals the hidden heart — a rewarding easter egg.
risk: At 32px the tiny heart cutout can shrink to a faint highlight.

title: Poincaré Diagonal
concept: The upright Julia triangle sits inside a faint 45° ellipse cloud with axes and an identity diagonal behind it.
why: Keeps the Julia triangle 100% intact while layering in genuine HRV semantics as background texture.
risk: At favicon size the axes/diagonal disappear, leaving just the triangle.

title: Sinus Spark
concept: Pulse rings radiate from the purple dot alone, casting it as the pacemaker (sinus node) that fires first.
why: The asymmetric energy source gives a clear focal point and a distinct silhouette from other ring marks.
risk: The pacemaker nuance may read simply as 'one big dot, two small' without context.

title: Monitor Grid
concept: A bedside-monitor bezel with a faint graph-paper grid behind an ECG trace whose three R-peaks are the Julia dots.
why: The rounded bezel + grid instantly signals 'clinical monitor', adding context the plain strip lacks.
risk: Most detail-dense mark; the grid fades to nothing at 32px — best used above favicon size.

title: Concentric Orbit
concept: Pulse rings ripple outward from a shared center; the triad rides the outermost ring — orbit and beat-propagation at once.
why: Concentric rings are extremely robust at small sizes and the triad sits confidently on top.
risk: The inner rings are decorative and could be dropped without hurting the concept.

title: Trail Triad
concept: Each dot trails a short comet-tail arc, all curling the same way, implying synchronized orbital motion.
why: Motion trails are an intuitive, low-cognitive-load way to say 'orbit' — the most dynamic mark in the lane.
risk: Pale trails can read as smudges/shadows at very small sizes.

title: Pulse Ring
concept: The rhythm strip bent into a closed loop (a recurring cardiac cycle) with clock-like ticks and the triad marking beats on the rim.
why: Only circular composition in the lane, nodding to the limit-cycle dynamics vocabulary.
risk: Weakest at reading 'heartbeat' first glance — leans toward 'Julia mark in a circle'.

title: Spiral Converge
concept: A spiral trajectory winds outward from center and settles onto the top purple dot — a phase-space path converging onto a limit cycle.
why: Directly illustrates the 'converging to a limit cycle' dynamics idea, distinct from the pure-ring marks.
risk: The delicate inner windings blur first below ~24px; the triad stays legible regardless.

title: R-Spike
concept: The purple dot grows a narrow triangular spike off its crown, turning the dot itself into the silhouette of an ECG R-peak.
why: One dot doing double duty as both 'Julia purple' and 'R-peak' — about as reductive as the idea can get.
risk: At small sizes the spike could soften into a flame/teardrop rather than an explicit ECG reference.

title: Breath Wave
concept: A slow sinusoid (respiratory sinus arrhythmia — breathing's modulation of heart rate) carries three beats at crest, midline, trough.
why: The only soft/organic register in the lane, giving range while staying grounded in real RSA physiology.
risk: A smooth wave alone can read 'signal/audio' more than 'heart' without the dot colors anchoring it.

title: Tachogram Steps
concept: A beat-to-beat interval series (tachogram) drawn as a jagged polyline; three of five vertices are the colored Julia dots, two are neutral anchors.
why: The zigzag height literally encodes IBI variability — exactly what a tachogram is.
risk: Could be mistaken for a generic line-chart icon without HRV context.

title: Ring Rhythm
concept: The three dots are open rings with a small Julia-blue pulse line threading the gaps between them like a beat passing through.
why: Outline dots + a wired pulse line is a genuinely different figure-ground treatment from every filled mark.
risk: Thin ring strokes and the blue squiggle are the most detail-dense; least margin for shrinking.

title: Loop Beat Heart
concept: The heart outline drawn as one continuous open stroke — purple left arc, green right — meeting at a red dot at the point.
why: Huge negative space reads immediately as a heart while feeling like a signal trace, not clip-art.
risk: Relies on the viewer completing the shape from an open contour.

title: Poincaré Cloud
concept: The honest Poincaré plot — NN(n) vs NN(n+1) samples scattered inside an elongated ellipse on the 45° identity line.
why: Instantly reads as 'Poincaré plot' to any HRV researcher — the field's single most iconic chart.
risk: At favicon size the scatter can read as a generic dotted blob.

title: R-Peak Bolt
concept: The QRS complex reduced to its single essential gesture — a bold Q-R-S zigzag, purple→blue gradient, no P/T waves.
why: The most abstracted, favicon-proof mark: thick, few points, unmistakable spike silhouette.
risk: Without P/T context some may read a generic 'lightning bolt'; leans on the blue accent more than most.

title: Pulse Tile
concept: A rounded-square app-icon tile in Julia purple with a bold white ECG trace knocked through the center.
why: Extremely legible at favicon size; the tile form factor is exactly what app icons are judged against.
risk: Single-color tile is the least 'Julia-coded' on its own; relies on family context.

title: Lorenz Wings
concept: The two-lobe topology of the Lorenz attractor stylized as one continuous infinity stroke crossing at the saddle point.
why: Captures the defining 'two wings, one crossing' structure in a single elegant stroke.
risk: Could read as a plain infinity symbol to viewers unfamiliar with the attractor.

title: Cleft Beat Heart
concept: A two-tone geometric heart (purple/green) whose natural top cleft bursts into a small red QRS zigzag.
why: The spike literally grows from the heart's own anatomy, so the beat is structural, not decorative.
risk: At very small sizes the thin spike can soften into a short tick.

title: Nested Cycles
concept: Two concentric orbits at very different scale — a big loose loop (green, high HRV) against a small tight loop (red, low HRV).
why: The size contrast alone tells the HRV story (bigger orbit = more variability) with no text.
risk: Could be misread as a plain target/bullseye without the HRV framing.

title: Pulse Emitter
concept: A compact red R-peak spike broadcasting three concentric rhythm waves outward in purple, green, and blue.
why: Reads as signal + transmission — exactly what HRV feature extraction is — distinct from every 'line in a box'.
risk: Off-center; at a glance could be mistaken for a wifi/signal icon if the red spike doesn't register first.

title: Faceted Heart
concept: A low-poly heart built from three flat color facets (purple, green, red) meeting at a shared center.
why: Sharp facet lines and flat blocking feel deliberately engineered/scientific rather than decorative.
risk: Can momentarily read as a shield or gem before 'heart' resolves.

title: Limit Cycle
concept: A Van der Pol relaxation-oscillator limit cycle drawn as a bold stadium-shaped orbit with a beat riding the trajectory.
why: A closed loop is the simplest, boldest way to say 'dynamical system in equilibrium' — clear even at 32px.
risk: A stadium shape alone could be mistaken for a rounded-rectangle icon.

title: SD Compass
concept: SD1 (short axis) and SD2 (long axis) — the two numbers every Poincaré analysis reports — abstracted into a caliper cross on the diagonal with a ghost ellipse and mean-NN dot.
why: Turns two abstract HRV metrics into an immediately legible crosshair mark, distinct from every ellipse-based logo.
risk: Without HRV context it can read as 'a green X', missing the SD1/SD2 reference.

title: Sonar Pulse
concept: A beat propagating outward as thick concentric rings (purple→blue→green) tightening toward a solid red core.
why: Pure radial symmetry and bold ring widths make it the most instantly 'pulse' and it holds perfectly at favicon size.
risk: Without a literal heart/ECG shape it reads 'pulse/signal' more than 'heart'.

title: Capsule Monitor
concept: A two-tone purple/green capsule tile with a bold white rhythm trace running through it.
why: The capsule silhouette is memorable while the white-on-color trace reads instantly as 'heart monitor'.
risk: The pill shape could read as 'medicine' without the trace doing the identifying work.

title: Return-Map Heart
concept: A return-map scatter deliberately arranged so the point cloud's silhouette reads as a heart.
why: Delivers a heart 'constructed from dots' while staying in the data/attractor vocabulary — a knowing wink.
risk: Least scientifically literal mark here; a purist could object no real return map looks like a heart.

title: QRS Line
concept: The honest P-QRS-T complex as a single confident stroke — no container, no ornament, Julia purple.
why: The single most literal 'this is an ECG' read in the set; survives any size or background.
risk: Single-color mark leans least on the Julia palette; could read as a generic health icon.

title: IBI Caliper
concept: Two R-peak spikes on a baseline with a double-headed arrow measuring the gap between them, like a dimension line.
why: This is literally what the package measures — nothing needs explaining to an HRV-literate viewer.
risk: The dashed guide lines are the thinnest elements; first to soften on print.

title: Tri-Lead Stack
concept: Three stacked rhythm-strip leads, one in each core Julia color, gesturing at multi-lead recording.
why: Reads as genuine biomedical-signal vocabulary while still delivering the 'three Julia colors' cue.
risk: At extreme miniaturization the three thin lanes have the least margin before merging.

title: Pulse Ellipses
concept: A heartbeat rippling outward along the Poincaré diagonal — three same-orientation ellipses of increasing size, decreasing opacity.
why: Merges 'pulse' and 'Poincaré diagonal' into one ripple mark, distinct from scatter or cross variants.
risk: The fainter outer rings can wash out at favicon size or on busy backgrounds.

title: Rhythm Ring
concept: A continuous monitoring loop of four quarter-arcs (one per Julia color) broken at the top by a single red R-peak spike.
why: Uses all four palette colors at once without a three-dot cliché; the segmented ring says 'continuous monitoring'.
risk: At small sizes reads more as a segmented-loader icon; the spike is the only cardiac cue.

title: Triangular Orbit
concept: One continuous asymmetric closed trajectory (a limit cycle) that visits three phase-space nodes in Julia's three colors.
why: Satisfies the three-color convention while staying unmistakably 'orbit', not 'logo triangle'.
risk: The closest B mark to Julia's own three-dot logo; needs the loop bold so it doesn't collapse to three dots.

title: Dot-Fused Heart
concept: Two big Julia dots (purple, green) sit exactly where a heart's lobes belong, fused, with red filling the point beneath.
why: The cleanest fusion in the project — reads as heart AND as two Julia dots simultaneously.
risk: Very low risk; mainly keep the ink outline crisp so the red sliver isn't lost when small.

title: Heart from a Heartbeat
concept: An abstract heart built entirely from a single bent ECG line (no valentine curves); lobes and dip marked by the three dots.
why: Satisfies 'heart glyph built from curves not cliché' directly, and is the most universally legible C mark.
risk: Closest to a generic heart-outline icon if the dots were ever removed or miscolored.

title: Tri-Slice Heart
concept: A solid heart cut into three Mercedes-style 120° wedges from its centroid — the triad *is* the heart, sliced.
why: Instant heart read; the straight radial cuts feel intentional/geometric and stay crisp at any size.
risk: Hard straight seams are less 'organic'; can scan as pie art before heart for some.

title: Negative Heart
concept: Three large solid Julia circles fuse into a clover badge with a heart punched out of the middle as negative space.
why: The cleverest negative-space use in the set — the heart is implied yet an outline keeps it instantly legible.
risk: Fast scanners may parse 'three overlapping circles' before the heart-shaped hole.

title: H♥L
concept: Bold 'H' and 'L' flank a geometric heart standing in for the middle of the name; a tiny dot cluster inside nods to a Poincaré cloud.
why: Strongest square wordmark — clean, bold, reads as letters+heart even at 32px; the I♥NY substitution is instantly parseable.
risk: The internal dot cloud is a bonus detail invisible below ~64px.

title: Poincaré Triad
concept: A tilted Poincaré ellipse cloud along the 45° identity line whose three densest clusters are the three Julia dots.
why: Honors the real SD1/SD2 ellipse geometry while making the dominant read exactly the Julia triad.
risk: Faint scatter dots vanish at 32px, leaving '3 dots in an ellipse'.

title: Tachogram Triad
concept: Three IBI bars of different heights rise from a baseline, each capped by a Julia dot, linked by a thin trend line.
why: Bar-chart language reads instantly as 'time-series data', grounding the triad in recognizable HRV output.
risk: Could be mistaken for a generic bar-chart icon if the colors were muted.

title: Three-Stroke Heart
concept: The heart drawn only as an outline, stitched from three thick rounded brush-stroke arcs in the three Julia colors.
why: Confident negative space; a very legible line-art heart that still telegraphs 'three Julia colors'.
risk: The two short top arcs could weaken at extreme small sizes if stroked too thin.

title: Triad Pulse Lockup
concept: The Julia three-dot triangle on an ECG baseline with a peak beneath, paired with the full 'HeartRateLab' wordmark.
why: The safest, most legible default lockup — Julia package + heartbeat + full name at a glance.
risk: The least novel of the lockups; closest in spirit to the reference seed.

title: Trefoil Pulse
concept: Three dot-derived teardrop petals meet at a small blue pulse-core, rotated 120° apart — a three-fold beat.
why: A clean, original silhouette unmistakably built from three equal colored parts meeting at one beating point.
risk: Reads as pulse/trefoil more than a literal heart — the weakest 'heart' read of its studio.

title: Pulse Ring
concept: A thin heart-monitor ring (ECG wrapped into a circle) with three radial pulse-blips 120° apart, each ending in a Julia dot.
why: Perfect rotational symmetry and a monitor-ring frame make 'pulse' unmistakable while the triad stays intact.
risk: The small radial ticks can fuse into the dots at 32px, reducing to 'ring + 3 dots'.

title: Radiating Pulse Heart
concept: Three nested heart contours scaling down to a solid red core, rippling outward like a pulse — rings reshaped as hearts.
why: An original combination of two brief motifs (pulse rings + heart) that reads neither generic nor cliché.
risk: The outer purple ring is the thinnest element; needs contrast at favicon size.

title: Limit-Cycle Knot
concept: An asymmetric organic closed loop (a Van der Pol relaxation-oscillation limit cycle, not a circle) with the three dots riding the trajectory at uneven points.
why: The lopsided non-circular contour reads distinctly as a dynamical-systems trajectory while still resolving into the triad.
risk: Without dynamics-literate context some viewers may just see 'a blob'.

title: R-Peak Letter Lockup
concept: A Van der Pol limit-cycle icon; in the wordmark the 'R' of 'Rate' is crowned by a sharp ECG spike on its cap.
why: Doubles Julia-native (blue accent, closed-loop dynamics) and HRV (R-peak) in one detail without hurting legibility.
risk: The crowned 'R' reads best at ≥200px wide; at tiny sizes it looks like an accent mark.

title: Orbiting Beat
concept: A small solid ink heart at center while the three Julia dots orbit it on a thin ring, like electrons around a nucleus.
why: A distinct atomic/orbital framing used nowhere else; the heart core stays legible even if the ring vanishes.
risk: The orbit ring and dots are the smallest elements; can lose contrast under 32px.

title: Spiral Attractor
concept: A true logarithmic phase-space spiral (a damped oscillator converging on a fixed point) with three passes marked by the three dots at decreasing radius.
why: Matches the brief's spiral vocabulary; the converging composition reads as 'settling into rhythm'.
risk: The multi-turn curve has the most path complexity; must stay thick-stroked to avoid muddiness when small.

title: Venn Pulse Heart
concept: Three translucent Julia-triad circles overlap inside a heart clip; their alpha-blended intersections nod to statistical Venn diagrams while the clip guarantees a heart.
why: The overlap/blend is a subtle wink at the package's statistical heritage, with a guaranteed heart silhouette.
risk: At very small sizes the blended overlaps can read a touch muddy.

title: Tri-Chrome HRL
concept: The initials H-R-L each set in one Julia color, underlined by a thick ECG line with a single R-peak spike under the 'R'.
why: Reads instantly as an acronym mark and a heartbeat trace at once; strong at large and favicon scale.
risk: Three letter colors could feel busy on a busy background; wants a neutral backdrop.

title: Petal Heart
concept: Three dot-derived teardrop petals — purple and green lobes, red point — overlap so their union reads as one continuous heart.
why: A softer, more organic heart than the wedge/Venn versions, still obviously built from three colored parts.
risk: The red petal is mostly hidden, showing only as a thin sliver — the third color can be missed at a glance.

title: Heart Badge Lockup
concept: A two-tone geometric heart paired with 'HeartRateLab' riding a continuous ECG baseline that bumps into an R-peak under 'Rate'.
why: The most approachable lockup — the heart reads instantly and the underline ties the ECG motif to the name itself.
risk: Leans most on the 'heart' cliché; kept honest by the bicolor split and ECG baseline.
